title: Training & Combat
status: Adopted24October2026: faction clock v2, range-band movement amendment2. Engaged/Short/Long/Out ranges and persistent movement intents; effort costs0/0.25/0.50/1.00 Endurance per15seconds. Metric combat movement, numeric reach and simulator clocks are outdated. Max Speed is narrative travel only.
rotationNote: Zero’s current defensive handling: one-time S240 starting assessments, not newly earned training. Percentages describe the response after a clean breakthrough has been denied or an interception opportunity selected, against an unfamiliar opponent with all responses feasible. Familiarity and actual openings change them. No stance is active outside combat.

sections.title: Learning & Mastery
sections.summary: Practice develops control, efficiency and reliability.
paragraphs: Credits = actual productive hours × training quality. Quality ranges from 0.25 to 25. A fully supported twelve-hour programme at quality 25 earns 300 credits; sixteen productive hours earn 400. There is no eight-hour credit cap. Sleep, meals and inactive breaks are not simultaneous practice.

Learning is below 10 credits; Learned starts at 10, Proficient at 250, Advanced at 2,500 and Mastered at 10,000. Thresholds promote automatically without an exam or promotion roll. Established feats remain valid; historical Developing/Practised labels do not automatically assign numerical tiers.

Intensity, feedback, challenge, live application, environment, recovery support, attention, transferable understanding and review contribute to quality. Fatigue, interfering injury, poor matching, technical error, distraction and hostile conditions reduce it. Advantages add rather than multiplying into a mandatory checklist. Many kinds of practice can develop the same skill.

Primary practice earns hours × quality. Supporting skills can receive 50%, 25% or 10% for strong, secondary or incidental involvement, totalling no more than 100% of primary work. No recursive credit. New combinations have 40 setup credits; original inventions 120; an established method has none. Later stages of an existing line do not repeat invention.

Before Learned, each genuine eligible combat execution with novice failure risk earns1 learning unit after resolution, successful or failed, capped at10. Use pre-attempt progress for the failure draw and a unique attempt ID to prevent repeated awards. Declarations, pellets and repeated ledger reads are not extra attempts. After Learned, ordinary combat use grants no automatic proficiency; dedicated practice including focused sparring still earns hours × quality, without double-counting the same work.

Training does not raise a transformation’s fixed multiplier. It improves activation, control, energy use and duration. Learning a new state still requires its recorded prerequisites. Reliable deliberate transformation combinations require mastery of the underlying methods and separate compatibility training; established feats and involuntary external access remain exceptions.

After mastery, refinement can continue more slowly. The proposed preparation/economy factor is R = 1 / (1 + 0.10 × log2(1 + extra credits / 10,000)). It never grants free energy, a stronger form factor or immunity to strain. Ordinary Power Level growth has a separate reviewed ledger; publishing this reference does not recalculate earlier gains.

sections.title: Kiai & Second Wind
sections.summary: Basic trained power gathering and recovery have their own progress.
paragraphs: Kiai belongs to Transformation & Amplification. Learned/Proficient/Advanced/Mastered caps add 25/50/75/100 percent of unamplified form power, with full gathering times180/120/90/60 seconds. Current output is base × form × (compatible amplifier + gathered bonus) × availability; count each layer once. Form or bodily-amplifier changes reset the gathered bonus.

At elapsed gathering time t, bonus = tier cap × (t / full time)^(2/3), capped at the tier limit. Upkeep is coefficient × bonus² per minute, with coefficients4/2/1/0.25 by tier, also accruing during gathering. Partial boosts are useful; competing attack preparation requires its own opening.

Ordinary Second Wind costs zero Endurance. It develops from one10-point recovery, to one15-point recovery, then two15-point recoveries, then two20-point recoveries. Restoration is fixed, with no recovery-amount roll. At zero, recovery takes45actual seconds with restoration at completion, retaining overflow; a qualifying100-plus hit bypasses it. Each spent reserve recharges24personally experienced hours after completion. Regenerative biology uses its own replacement profile.

Zero has existing Proficient Kiai750 and Second Wind650, assessed from the player correction and recorded training. These are starting assessments, not new elapsed training. Guru’s potential release improves strength, speed, resilience and absolute endurance; technique proficiency remains separately trained. The fresh100-point endurance scale is relative to that stronger body.

sections.title: Tolerance & Recovery
sections.summary: Harder work earns progress; recovery determines how long it stays sustainable.
paragraphs: Carry tolerance T, unrecovered strain D, highest attained tolerance H and maintenance gap N. T and H cannot exceed 20; passive tolerance loss stops at 5. Personal-best memory is retained. These are fictional campaign measures, not human sleep guidance.

Light, normal, hard and intensive practice create 0.25, 0.50, 0.75 and 1.00 load per productive hour. Recovery capacity C = T × min(1, recovery hours / 8) × (0.75 + 0.125 × support), where support is 0–2. Closing D = max(0, opening D + load − C). The next session’s quality deduction is min(4, D / 2). Do not count the same fatigue twice or erase it at midnight.

Use actual completed recovery, not a promised night’s sleep. Ordinary productive and protected recovery hours do not overlap; an explicitly restorative body has the exception below. A mixed programme may be easier to sustain than continuous intensive work; no compulsory physical/mental activity split is imposed.

Demanding effort E = sum(hours × intensity / 3), with intensity 0–3. Recovered adaptation budget a = 0.1 × E × min(1, C / (opening D + load)); no load or recovery gives no adaptation. First-time tolerance grows as sqrt(T² + a). Below the recorded personal best, only the portion rebuilding H gains four times that squared-growth budget; growth beyond H returns to the normal rate.

Maintenance anchors: T5 needs 0.5 effort per week with 30 unsupported grace days; T10 needs 2 with 14 days; T15 needs 7 with 7 days; T20 needs 14 with 2 days. Interpolate between anchors. Meaningful contested combat supplies 0.2 × intensity / 3 per exchange, capped at 2 daily maintenance units, without creating imaginary practice hours or counting a counter twice.

Use training effort plus only combat maintenance not already counted by its actual duration. Daily requirement M is weekly demand / 7. Coverage = activity / M. Update N = min(grace + 1, max(0, previous N + 1 − coverage)). Beyond grace, lose 0.05 × max(0, 1 − coverage) tolerance that day, with a floor of 5. Full maintenance stops loss; returning to a former peak is faster, not instant. Skills and base power are not removed by tolerance decay.

An embodied-dead Other World body or explicitly equivalent restorative effect recovers training strain at 0.50 + T / 80 per actual hour, including practice. During protected rest use the greater ordinary/passive rate for overlapping hours, never both. At T12, twenty-four hours recover 15.6: Normal training creates 12 load, Hard 18, Intensive 24. Normal work can therefore clear old strain while harder work can accumulate it. Actual hours still earn credits; T stays capped at 20. A living visitor or sleep-removal-only wish does not automatically gain this recovery. It does not heal every wound or refill all combat energy.

sections.title: Attacks, Defence & Counters
sections.summary: One breakthrough check, then a defence response when needed.
paragraphs: Physical Combat (legacy ID combat-basics, formerly Combat Fundamentals) covers ordinary punches, kicks and close-range strikes: a flurry of lighter blows, fewer heavy blows or one committed heavy strike use the same bounded-attempt profile. Ki Blasts (legacy ID ki-blast) covers ordinary unnamed shots, volleys, concentrated blasts and beams, including mouth-fired blasts where that fighter has the handling. These are narrative delivery variations, with identical damage, expenditure, multiplier and engagement accounting at the same skill tier; fewer blows do not add a heavy-attack bonus or divide the damage. Actual limbs, range and firing path still determine feasibility. Distinct methods such as Kamehameha, Special Beam Cannon and the recorded Break Cannon retain their own profiles; an ordinary mouth blast does not acquire those properties. Each attempt resolves once, never once per depicted hit or pellet.

Meaningfully contested combat uses automatic private, saved rolls for everyone. Fix intent, actual capabilities, supply, timing, range, injuries and feasible outcomes first. Impossible and certain results need no random draw. No rerolls, lucky minimum chance, protagonist padding or retrospective bonuses.

For attack aiming, use the Power Level available for that action, excluding a technique-bound bonus. With r the ratio, t=min(1,abs(ln r)/ln4), w=r^(0.5+1.5t²); r0 gives0. Apply independent agility², skill, position and directional familiarity once. Chance=w/(1+w). This retained close-gap curve reaches the squared curve at fourfold gaps. Damage still scales linearly with the Power Level during the technique.

After a failed clean breakthrough, a secondary draw chooses guard, dodge, parry or a counter opportunity. An interception response remains pending until collision. Neutral weights are 50/25/15/10. Trained rotations change that conditional distribution; they are not another chance to reverse a successful hit. Remove impossible responses before rolling and normalise the remaining weights.

A Counter transfers half the current attack segment under clock v2; ordinary Guard does not. The transferred interval is debited from its initiator and credited only to the responding fighter. It may fund a feasible response; an attack pays ordinary costs and uses ordinary accuracy. No separate free attack, whole new turn or duplicate global time.

Physical counters use a ready Physical signature or style-appropriate strikes; Ki counters use a suitable Ki signature or ordinary Ki Blast variation. A response never copies an unknown move or receives free charge. A feasible Ki interception can start a clash: test uncertain interception once, then compare actual delivered powers. Collision is not a free hit on the caster. A weaker response may be overrun.

Working convention: one signature attack per active form/loadout, with optional form overrides referencing already learned moves. Physical and Ki attacks qualify; Transformation & Amplification and Discipline do not. It is a default preference, not a limit on choosing other attacks. Zero defaults to Spirit Spear when ready and in contact range; ordinary physical combinations or Ki Blast volleys/spheres cover other windows. Spirit Bomb is not a reliable emergency signature, and a maximum-power basic blast gains no invented multiplier.

An exchange groups a tight combination or bounded rapid-blast volley, not damage per fist or pellet. One root combination and its immediate counter chain earns one readable familiarity/maintenance exposure; every actual attempted attack still costs endurance. Changed tactics, supply, positions or genuinely subsequent attacks create new windows.

sections.title: Endurance & Exertion
sections.summary: Ordinary exchanges accumulate wear; heavy techniques spend more energy.
paragraphs: At positive Endurance E, availability=1-0.4*((100-E)/90)^2; at10 it is60%, at50 about87.65%. At0 effective combat awaits a valid recovery. Apply this once; a technique multiplier never becomes a defensive buff. Use a fresh 100-point combat-endurance reference, tracking received wear and unrecovered offensive exertion separately. This is campaign bookkeeping, not a percentage of Power Level or a newly measured current reserve. Actual injuries and pre-existing fatigue remain relevant; transformation does not refresh it.

Physical Combat governs ordinary physical combinations; Ki Blast governs ordinary Ki combinations. At Learned/Proficient/Advanced/Mastered, complete clean body-parity damage is 3/4/5/6. Physical costs are 1.00/0.75/0.60/0.50; Ki costs are 1.50/1.25/1.00/0.85 per bounded attempt, including misses. Use the current tier row between thresholds. Scale damage by delivered output / defensive bodily output; a feasible guard transmits 20%, full evasion/parry none.

Beyond mastery, ordinary damage stays at 6 while cost uses diminishing refinement R. There is no extra accuracy, Power Level, per-punch or per-pellet bonus. Do not add Ki Control or ordinary mastery again to a named technique. Unmigrated current credits preserve the earlier 4 damage / 0.75 physical / 1.25 Ki accounting baseline, explicitly not a Proficient assignment. Established feats remain valid; explicitly below-Learned execution needs its own recorded profile.

A technique temporarily raises the user’s one Power Level for its duration. Compare that Power Level with the defender through power-gap scaling, then apply fixed intrinsic damage and actual defence. The technique-bound increase ends with the technique and cannot enhance unrelated punches, movement or defence. Intrinsic values before Mastered / at Mastered: Kamehameha5/6, Galick Gun5/6, Spirit Spear8.5/9.5, Super Kamehameha7/8, Final Flash9/10, Cannon14/15 and Spirit Bomb19/20. Named Ki methods lose1 from their former pre-Mastered base; Spirit Spear has the same explicit correction. Every named Physical/Ki method gains1 once at Mastered. Ordinary attacks retain their own existing ladder. Never interpolate or repeatedly award this bonus. Current operational scaling is delivered output / defensive bodily output. Never add another charge multiplier to damage. Endurance expenditure is calculated separately.

Ordinary profiled beams/wave and Spirit Spear use coefficient × technique factor² × economy (Cannon and Spirit Bomb use their distinct profiles below): coefficient 1.5 for Galick Gun, 2 for the other profiled self-powered beams/wave, 1 for Spirit Spear handling plus its actual donated energy. Economy anchors are 1/0.85/0.65/0.45 at Learned/Proficient/Advanced/Mastered; do not invent a tier to grant a discount. Mastered Galick Gun costs 6.075 at regular ×3 and 24.3 at full ×6, a 25% reduction; intrinsic damage is5 before Mastered and6 at Mastered before power-gap scaling. Preparation and sustain use the same reduced expenditure profile.

Accrue regular cost through preparation and add actual overcharge cost; release does not pay twice. Interrupted attempts retain spent effort. Sustained beams add one release cost per explicit interval: Kamehameha120seconds, Galick Gun180, Super Kamehameha120, Final Flash180, Cannon180. Faster preparation does not change these upkeep intervals. A recorded replenishing source can override ordinary depletion within its limits.

Twenty equal-output clean Proficient physical exchanges cause 80 wear and cost 15; Mastered equivalents cause 120 and cost 10. These totals do not guarantee twenty connections or survival. Track losses and actual restoration in order, retaining separate received-wear and expenditure entries. Lifetime damage subtracted from 100 alone is invalid after recovery. Zero is exhaustion, not automatic death or unconsciousness. No automatic refill on a new exchange or form.

sections.title: Recovery & Lasting Damage
sections.summary: Major recovery takes45seconds; full regeneration is immediate.
paragraphs: Check each actual impact after Power Level scaling and resolved defence, before clipping it to remaining Endurance, applying passive regeneration or spending recovery reserves. At 100 or more Endurance damage, a target without true immortality dies immediately if the attack has killing intent; with nonlethal intent the target is immediately unconscious and incapacitated. Neither major nor full recovery can intervene. Fix intent before resolution. Cell/Buu-style regeneration alone is not true immortality. True immortality retains its recorded recovery, subject to the existing Zeno-level or specific reality-erasure exception. Separate impacts never pool toward100; expenditure and upkeep are not injury. Below100, an actually lethal wound can still kill. Ordinary zero alone remains exhaustion, not automatic unconsciousness or death.

Major partial recoveries, including Second Wind and Namekian-style repair, take 45 actual seconds at every tier and Power Level. Record start and completion deadline; restore the fixed amount only on completion. At zero the fighter cannot fight, maintained voluntary forms drop immediately and unsupported holds/preparations end. An ally can buy time; no protection prevents an enemy finishing the casualty. Full regeneration is immediate and can preserve an active state if it restores viable Endurance before collapse. Recovery has no Endurance cost.

Below the terminal-hit rule, apply an established passive injury refund once, then subtract loss. At zero use an available suitable full regeneration first and carry remaining damage through it immediately. Otherwise reserve one eligible major recovery for its45-second deadline and retain the unpaid overflow. At completion subtract that overflow from the fixed restore; if exhausted again, another available major recovery needs its own45seconds. Never discard excess or apply passive refund again. Pending recovery does not fund attacks. Reserve the slot while pending, spend it and start its existing cooldown when restoration completes; cancellation releases the unused reservation. Further injury is resolved when it lands and its excess persists; it does not silently restart the deadline. Death, terminal incapacitation or loss of the actual regenerative mechanism cancels pending restoration. External healing that resolves the depletion cancels the unspent pending recovery without a duplicate restore; it does not reset spent slots.

The existing75 retained-damage trigger remains for surviving hits leaving1–20; at zero full regeneration takes priority.35−50 with a full reserve ends85 immediately; with only a20-point major recovery it ends5 after45seconds. Existing reserve sizes and cooldowns remain. Ordinary Second Wind slots recharge24subjective hours after use, never on a new fight or ordinary Senzu.

Nonlethal100-plus incapacitation has no automatic45-second wake-up. An ally may reach and rouse the casualty where their condition allows; waking alone heals no injury and restores no Endurance. Record the actual intervention and remaining condition. A subsequent recovery requires regained eligibility, not an automatic escape from incapacitation. Lethal bodily destruction is distinct from body-and-soul erasure under DEATH-AND-REVIVAL.md.

sections.title: Rotations & Remembered Opponents
sections.summary: Training shapes your response; experience with an opponent improves your read.
paragraphs: Each rotation retains its own cumulative progress. Neutral weights are50/25/15/10. Multiply its preferred baseline by1.5/2/3/4 at Learned/Proficient/Advanced/Mastered, then by1+F/500 for applicable familiarity. Filter impossible modes and normalise. Guard specialists remain more reliable than equally trained Dodge, Parry and Counter specialists. Old target-blending is replay-only.

Familiarity is directional and ranges from 0 to 100. For each attacking pair, multiply ordinary odds by (800 + attacker familiarity) / (800 + defender familiarity). Equal familiarity cancels this primary advantage, while both retain their defensive rotation benefit. Complete familiarity against none changes an otherwise equal contest from 50% to about 52.94%, not a guaranteed hit.

Each readable root exchange grants 0.10/0.15/0.20/0.25/0.30 familiarity points at Learning/Learned/Proficient/Advanced/Mastered reading proficiency. Use the highest recorded rotation tier as the initial proxy. Award once after resolution, only for what that observer could perceive. Rebuilding below the retained peak is twice as fast for that portion only. Forty readable roots at Mastered add 12 points to a new read; reaching 100 from zero takes 334 without rust or timing changes. Gains apply between roots, so adaptation occurs during combat while lasting familiarity develops across repeated encounters. Existing remembered scores are retained; counter chains do not multiply awards.

Memory persists between encounters. After 30 personally experienced days without relevant contact, familiarity loses one point per seven further days, down to a quarter of its retained peak. Base growth scales the old timing read by min(1, saved ordinary base / current ordinary base), once from its saved anchor. Small growth causes a small adjustment; it does not erase remembered facts.

An unfamiliar form, technique or genuinely changed approach gets its own record. Known approaches remain retrievable, adjusted for rust and base growth. Missing records require checking the story, not assigning amnesia. Opposing directions and different timeline counterparts never share scores automatically.

Intent selects a learned rotation: buying time or distance favours Evasive; holding a line Bulwark; redirecting Deflection; baiting a reply Riposte. Otherwise retain the compatible approach or Neutral. No compulsory menu or artificial action cost; combat movement follows persistent intent and effort without off-turn time debt. Mastered targets remain bounded even with full familiarity.

sections.title: Allies & Multiple Attackers
sections.summary: Coordination divides attention without adding bodies into one power level.
paragraphs: For genuinely simultaneous attacks, calculate each attacker’s own weight and familiarity factor. First-breakthrough chance = sum(weights) / (1 + sum(weights)). Choose the first breakthrough in proportion to those weights, then reassess still-viable follow-ups. Sequential attacks do not automatically overload defence.

Actual crossfire can multiply weights by 1.5 when it forces incompatible defensive movements. Headcount alone does not earn it. Two equal unfamiliar attackers have 66.67% first-breakthrough odds, or 75% with genuine crossfire. Other ratios use the current close-gap curve, not old squared-curve examples.

Never pool familiarity or give everyone the best teammate’s read. The defender’s conditional rotation uses a separate joint-pattern record. One failed shared contest produces one defence draw; a feasible counter transfers time from one initiating attacker, not the entire team. Remaining threats may make a counter impossible. Very weak crowds receive no artificial chance floor or guaranteed chip damage.

sections.title: Protected Charges & Allied Injury
sections.summary: Allies buy real time; a missed shot can still hit the protector.
paragraphs: Adopted23October2026. Screen or contest the approach while an ally charges, then time any final restraint from resolved Engaged access, grip attempts, orientation and the remaining charge window. Each attempt and escape requires real time and expenditure. No mandatory pin, universal three-second hold, team penalty or compulsory idle time. Positioning uses fatigue-reduced bodily output and effort; preparation remains mastery-timed.

Clear the actual firing lane after a perceptible cue, including the risk of a protector behind the target. A prepared Cannon may wait while stationary, vulnerable and paying its existing sustain rate; waiting grants no extra charge or second release bill. An enemy can flank, escape, counter or change target when actually able. A grip restricts only the motion it controls.

After evasion, follow the released projectile to its next actual body or obstacle, regardless of allegiance. A newly exposed protector has only the actual warning-to-arrival window to react and complete a feasible defence. With no time or route, contact is certain; otherwise use ordinary saved resolution for that recipient. Do not reuse the original target’s defence or automatically retaliate against the allied caster.

An allied hit uses the same fixed intrinsic damage, released Power Level, recipient output and resolved defence. Apply ordinary received wear, zero-cost recovery and all overflow; no friendly-fire discount, duplicate multiplier or second attack cost. Actual wounds and survival remain distinct from Endurance. A clean disruptive impact can interrupt preparation or break restraint, with spent effort retained; guarded or glancing contact need not cancel every action.

After the100-damage terminal check and immediate full regeneration/overflow, unrecovered zero ends effective fighting and maintained voluntary forms. Major recovery remains pending45seconds. Release unsupported holds and cancel preparation. Later healing does not automatically reactivate a form; existing residual access and actual involuntary triggers retain their own conditions. Accidental allied contact earns no extra familiarity. Save the original shot, contact, injury and recovery records through any interruption.

Learned Cannon remains situational:300seconds regular preparation,480seconds total maximum. Higher Cannon timing anchors now follow the15second table; Kiai’s profile, gathering times and costs remain unchanged. The live procedure is adopted; synthetic grip coefficients, timestep sizes and reported win rates are not universal rules. Historical tests that harmlessly removed a shot on allied contact are superseded.

sections.title: Charge Windows & Beam Clashes
sections.summary: Preparing more power creates an opening an opponent can contest.
paragraphs: ## Faction turns and concurrent engagements

Each faction receives45 seconds. Every member acts concurrently within that window, not45 seconds per combatant. Each fighter has their own commitments; actions taken by one do not consume another's time. Each faction window advances the shared elapsed clock45seconds once. Two factions therefore complete a round in90seconds. No attack is retroactively intercepted on the next faction turn: resolve feasible defensive reactions and existing protection before its outcome is final. A faction turn is a resolution window; prose may interleave the exchange naturally without rewriting resolved events.

Separated engagements retain the same round and global timestamps. Resolve their overlapping windows concurrently and advance only to the latest shared deadline, never sum the duration of separate duels. Rejoining requires accessible range bands, a viable route and defeating or evading an opponent's interception under the movement-intent rule. New arrivals join the current window with only its remaining time. Existing preparation, recovery, movement and upkeep continue during hostile windows where compatible; starting a new offensive commitment normally uses the actor's own faction window or transferred counter time. Record each local faction order before resolution.
## Commitments and preparation

Ordinary Physical Combat or Ki Blasts take30seconds per bounded attempt at every tier. A heavy strike and a flurry are narrative variants of the same profile. Named techniques use their own recorded preparation time INCLUDING execution/release. Full Charge is total time from start, not additional time. Never add a generic delivery, planning, engagement or release charge. Compatible range movement overlaps preparation without another approach or projectile-travel commitment. Delivery still requires a valid range band and path.

Activation and named-use times are15-second multiples fixed by the current tier. No fractional interpolation of these times. Zero is permitted only for expressly instant Mastered activation or residual reactivation. Post-mastery timing refinement rounds upward to15seconds with a15second minimum for attacks; a recorded instant activation stays zero. Costs retain their existing interpolation/refinement. Charges may carry across turns, with actual paid progress retained. Interrupted work retains expenditure and loses only preparation actually disrupted. A technique cannot be banked through unrelated attacks.

At Zero's present progress Kaioken x2 activates in15seconds and Spirit Spear takes45seconds for regular use or120seconds total full charge. Activating Kaioken and then regular Spear takes60seconds, so cannot both finish in an ordinary45-second turn. Kaioken then an ordinary30-second attack can fit. Spirit Bomb remains Learning:120seconds minimum release and630seconds full with adequate supply. No ability, credits or story time are granted by this migration.
## Counters transfer time

Keep the existing conditional Guard/Dodge/Parry/Counter weights. Only a Counter result transfers time; ordinary Guard does not. A counter establishes a feasible defensive opening, not a free attack or guaranteed hit. The defender takes half the interrupted attack's currently contested commitment: a30second ordinary attack gives15seconds; a15second attack gives7.5seconds. Long preparation does not become hundreds of bonus seconds: use at most the current45second segment, excluding earlier completed preparation. Maximum transfer22.5seconds per selected counter.

Resolve the counter within that attack segment: its first half is the defensive contest, the second half becomes the defender's response time. Debit that exact interval from the initiating attacker's commitment and credit it to the responding fighter. The transfer changes ownership of existing time, not the global clock. The defender may act immediately during it; if they carry a charge into their following45second faction window, their combined opportunity is60 or52.5seconds in the examples. Preserve7.5 exactly. Do not round it to52 or secretly give another attack. A gap occupied by other combatants between these windows remains real and interruptible.

Counter time may support preparation, repositioning, support, defence or an attack that actually fits. Each new attack pays its normal cost and uses ordinary accuracy. It can itself produce a counter, transferring only remaining unspent time in its current segment; no time can be transferred twice or minted by a counter chain. A failed long attack retains prior preparation costs. Other combatants retain their own commitments and may intervene. Counter transfer does not freeze the enemy faction or give every ally bonus time. Persist source interval, recipient, amount and spent remainder under the original exchange ID. Automatic modest responses follow established fighting style; do not choose a major player transformation, consumable or target without authorisation.
## Defence, support and intentional knockback

A dedicated defensive turn forgoes initiating attacks and multiplies the selected rotation's preferred weight by1.5 before feasibility filtering/normalisation, alongside the existing mastery and familiarity factors. Neutral distributes the benefit across Guard and Dodge proportionally. It grants no immunity. Counter time on a defensive turn can sustain defence, move or support; changing to offence ends this bonus before resolving the attack. Repositioning, retreat, protecting a route and supporting an ally are legitimate alternatives to attacking. A reachable accessible Senzu, fruit consumption or attempt to rouse an ally takes15seconds after range access is established; real impediments still matter. An energy donation uses its recorded transfer method/rate and actual supply, not an automatic refill.

A successful intentional launching knockback produces15seconds of stagger for arresting momentum, bracing, extracting oneself from rubble and regaining control. Declare the launch as the intended consequence before the contest. Ordinary contact, a glancing guard or piercing alone does not guarantee it. Record the actual resulting location and obstacles; returning uses the range-band movement rule after stagger. Stagger prevents voluntary new preparation/offence and interrupts concentration where the hit actually disrupts it; allies and available automatic regeneration still operate. Do not stack repeated overlapping stagger into an unlimited bank. A new consequential impact can establish a new15second deadline from that hit. Apply the same rules to the player and enemies.
## Range-band movement — amendment2

Adopted24October2026 from the player's accepted range-band review. Combat ranges are **Engaged → Short → Long → Out of Combat Range**. They describe tactical access amid continuous high-speed movement, not fixed metre boundaries. Engaged permits contact; Short permits ordinary ranged exchanges; Long requires a dedicated ranged technique. Out ends immediate attack access, not observation, pursuit through the story or the possibility of rejoining. Actual cover, firing lanes, restraints and separated groups still matter.

**Persistent movement intent.** Select intent and effort on the fighter's own turn, using their declared plan, then retain them like a defensive rotation until changed on a later own turn. Close Distance seeks one band closer. Make Distance seeks one band farther. Maintain Range preserves the chosen band relative to the relevant opponent, moving reactively when necessary. Hold Position preserves a location or stationary preparation and does not automatically chase. An intent is not permission to change the player's target or abandon their preparation. Record the relevant opponent/route when several threats exist; nobody can occupy contradictory positions or protect every route merely by declaring an intent. Actual incapacitation or an incompatible stationary task removes an unavailable response without substituting a new tactic.

**One interaction per pair per faction window.** Resolve the acting movement and one automatic response together; never stop for an extra movement-choice exchange. Both Close from Long gives Long→Short→Engaged. Both Make Distance from Short gives Short→Long→Out. Clamp at the end bands. Compatible movements resolve without an unnecessary roll. Maintain against a change or Close against Make Distance produces one opposed positioning roll. Hold Position supplies no movement contest; actual restraint or an impassable route still controls feasibility. No recursive chase responses or new movement roll for every blow, counter or projectile. Store the pair/window result; a counter uses the existing positioning result unless an actual impact changes the situation, not a fresh attempt to fish for better positioning.

**Opposed result.** A successful initiator establishes the intended adjacent band; a failure lets the responder preserve its selected range/current band. Failed withdrawal leaves the existing band and does not cancel an attack already valid there. A failed adjacent approach can still reach fleeting delivery contact: resolve the declared attack automatically at **half its normal attack odds weight**, then return to the defender's preferred band unless the actual hit causes a different consequence such as launching or restraint. This is not half damage or half the final hit percentage: weight1 becomes0.5, giving33⅓% instead of50%; weight3 becomes1.5, giving60% instead of75%. Apply the penalty once to that attack, alongside its normal directional familiarity. It grants no new attack or lasting Engaged position. Long→Short alone cannot deliver melee; the fleeting-contact exception only applies when the attempted one-band approach would reach the technique's permitted band. Failed movement does not require another player prompt.
**Effort and cost.** These percentages are effort settings, not fractions of Max Speed. Freeze the selected setting before resolving an interaction.

| Movement effort | Endurance per15seconds | Per45seconds continuously moving | Positioning weight |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
|25%|0|0|0.5|
|50%|0.25|0.75|1|
|75%|0.50|1.50|1.5|
|100%|1.00|3.00|2|

Accrue movement expenditure once through actual ongoing deliberate movement, on either faction's window. Record start/stop and paid-through times, split at impacts, recovery, stagger and state changes, and prorate incomplete intervals. Continuing movement across two full windows costs twice the45second amount; a second opponent or a second roll does not add another fee over the same interval. Merely retaining an intent while not moving costs nothing. Hold Position costs zero movement; ordinary guard/dodge footwork is already included in its action. Involuntary knockback costs no voluntary movement expenditure. Form upkeep and attack preparation retain their separate existing costs. Endurance is paid whether an opposed movement succeeds or fails.

**Positioning arithmetic.** Use current available bodily Power Level, excluding technique-bound output. For positive ratio r=initiator/responder, t=min(1,abs(ln(r))/ln(4)); weight=r^(0.5+1.5*t*t) × initiator effort weight / responder effort weight × independently recorded agility ratio². Probability=weight/(1+weight). Use agility1 unless an independent combat-agility difference is recorded; travelCoefficient and the power-derived speed ratio are not agility. No extra familiarity, generic skill or improvised position bonus is added to this positioning roll; existing familiarity remains in attack/defence. Actual route/limb/awareness restrictions determine feasibility first. Incapacitated movement is impossible, not a tiny lucky chance. Fix output and circumstances once for the interaction; tiny costs during it do not trigger repeated movement rolls. Save actual live draws via the existing private resolve procedure; worked examples are not draws or story gains.

At equal bodily output/agility against50% effort, the four effort settings give33⅓%,50%,60%,66⅔%. Equal efforts give50%. These are campaign coefficients accepted in the review, not canonical probabilities. Fatigue, actual forms and recovery affect bodily output through the existing availability rule; the same output is not counted again through travel speed.

**Time and preparation.** Reactive range movement creates no off-turn time debt, deducts nothing from a later turn, and adds no mandatory15second approach/delivery commitment. It accompanies the faction window and an actually compatible action. Stationary preparation cannot follow a moving intent while continuing to charge; it retains Hold Position until a later authorised change or actual interruption. Mobile Spirit Spear preparation may approach, but cannot include unrelated attacks. Counters transfer only the existing attack-segment time under the unchanged rule above; movement never mints extra offensive time. Actual obstacles, disabled movement or a failed range approach remain relevant without converting them into an automatic future-turn bill.

**Knockback.** A successful intentional launch retains15seconds of real stagger from impact, covering arresting momentum, normal rubble and regaining control. Record the consequent band and any real obstacle from the declared/resolved launch; do not invent a universal kilometre distance. Carry only the remaining stagger at a turn boundary. After it ends, return uses intent/range resolution with its ordinary effort cost; there is no added15second return manoeuvre. An actual additional obstacle can prevent access but the same rubble is never charged twice. Form drain continues during stagger.

**Technique ranges.** The following bands replace numeric combat reach at every tier; mastery still controls the method's existing handling, charge and costs. A valid band does not bypass cover, line of fire, functional limbs or a method-specific restriction.

| Method | Permitted delivery bands |
| --- | --- |
|Physical Combat and contact Physical Techniques, including Spirit Spear and Wolf Fang Fist|Engaged|
|Ki Blasts, including ordinary unnamed beams/volleys|Engaged, Short|
|Dedicated Beam/Heavy Beam/Piercing Beam techniques, including Kamehameha, Galick Gun and Special Beam Cannon|Engaged, Short, Long|
|Recorded named Projectile/Mouth Beam signature families|Engaged, Short, Long|
|Spirit Bomb, including Learning attempts|Short, Long|

New methods need an explicit range-band entry before deployment. Existing projected signature families inherit their listed family, not an invented unique range; ordinary mouth-fired Ki Blasts remain in the ordinary Ki Blasts row. Giants/extended limbs require their actual recorded contact capability, not silent access to all bands. No attack here reaches Out of Combat Range. Release follows resolved range/access and existing preparation, without a separate speed-based projectile clock. Projectiles retain their bearing and released power; no automatic homing or harmless disappearance on allied contact. Resolve feasible defence/interception within the committed attack window before finalising impact. A protector needs established access and a viable lane, not a retroactive next-turn rescue. Continuing shots retain their original release ID and ordinary allied-injury rules.

**Travel only.** Max Speed retains its narrative travel anchor:24000m/s × sqrt(current bodily power/8000) × individual travel coefficient × state mobility. It can answer journey/deadline questions outside combat, never positioning odds, band transitions, approach time, projectile timing or reaction seconds in combat. Combat does not use metres/speed, acceleration ramps, braking phases or the old minimum relocation commitment. The earlier numeric reach tables and metric pursuit/closure examples are outdated. Preserve those snapshots as history, not alternative current rules.
## Forms, costs and recovery

Forms have an activation time and one ongoing Endurance/minute rate, never a fixed active-duration limit. Drain starts on activation completion and is prorated across every actual second, including hostile turns, talking, charging and stagger. There is no activation fee or exertion surcharge. A Senzu replenishes according to its recorded effect and extends affordable use; it does not restart a fictitious duration timer. Split accounting at impacts, healing, activation, release and zero. Channel's8/4/2/1 and Kaioken x2's12/6/3/1.5 tier rates retain their cost interpolation. Uncontrolled remains0. Kiai formula, buildup and costs remain unchanged.

At unrecovered zero voluntary states drop. An immediate full regeneration can prevent collapse; a major recovery takes45seconds and grants no protection. Same-state reactivation within900seconds inclusive of the last exit is immediate when able, including after exhaustion. It resumes upkeep and restores neither Kiai nor attack charge. A single post-defence100-plus impact applies the existing lethal/nonlethal terminal rule before recoveries, with the existing true-immortality exception. None of these universal rules needs a repeated app field under every form.
## Beam clashes and interruptions

Counterbeam preparation must fit actual available time or already-carried preparation; a counter does not conjure a charged beam. Resolve geometry and the original threat before claiming it stopped. Once comparable sustained beams meet, use the actual remaining faction/counter windows for compatible extra charge, a usable transformation/amplifier, an accessible fruit or actual donation. Newly supplied output changes the clash; detached energy does not. The stronger beam pushes and an overwhelming one can resolve before a reply is feasible. Record the collision position and the next deadline before resolution. No guaranteed reply, automatic endless clash, or duplicate attack damage from an interception. A mouth blast conflicts with eating. Kiai retains180/120/90/60seconds; Learned Cannon retains300seconds regular and480seconds full.
## Persistence and combat footer

Persist global elapsed seconds, round/faction order, each engagement's shared timestamps, each actor's commitments and remaining work, pairwise range bands, relevant routes/cover, persistent intent and selected effort, pair/window movement-result IDs, actual moving intervals and movement paid-through time, actual impact/stagger deadline, current Endurance/injuries/state, upkeep paid-through time, charge supply, recovery deadlines and per-state last exit. Counter transfers retain interval IDs and spent time. Resolve earlier impacts/depletion without billing the whole pending interval. A narrative reply does not restart a turn. No simulations or retrospective duration padding.

NARRATOR-GUIDE.md section3 owns the separate Character Info and Combat Info presentation contract. Combat Info shows elapsed seconds, faction turn, each tracked combatant's Endurance/state/injuries, named pairwise bands, current ongoing drain and labelled damage/expenditure/recovery changes. Display Endurance figures rounded down to one decimal; retain full precision internally. Anchor elapsed combat to the actual local/timeline clock, carry residual seconds and display ordinary time to the minute. Advance each shared interval once, including concurrent engagements; counter transfers create no extra time. Keep mechanical numbers and rolls out of narrative prose. The former single-line Zero-only footer is superseded.

An observed opposing transformation prompts tactical reassessment outside beam clashes as well as within them. A fighter may answer with an actually available form, using real reaction and activation time, existing costs and a workable opening. Ongoing incompatible tasks, interruption and insufficient time still matter; entering a new form is not protected and does not refill Endurance. A committed activation remains tracked if its prompting clash ends. This neither grants a matching form nor forces every fighter to transform; player-controlled escalation remains the player’s choice. Kiai, power scaling and positioning are unchanged.

Power Level during the technique = ordinary base × total active-state factor × available fraction × technique factor. Count each effect once. A Kaioken combination uses its already-combined state factor; do not multiply Kaioken again. Transformation mastery does not increase that factor.

Protection requires resolved range access, firing lanes and the current attack window. Ordinary projectiles retain a release bearing/observed lead rather than automatically tracking targets. A mobile-compatible dodge preserves charge; stationary preparation cannot. Parry can redirect toward another enemy, never its originator, with ordinary defence for the new recipient. A counter transfers time under the faction clock; each chosen action must fit and pays its own cost. No arbitrary team-size penalty or free teleport.

A counterbeam can protect the user or an ally if awareness, orientation, path and preparation fit the incoming attack’s remaining preparation and available faction/counter window. Faster fighters can interrupt an activation or charge; allies can buy time. Use the45second faction clock; no automatic cinematic protection.

At collision compare actual delivered output and supply. Close clashes can allow response windows: a learned amplification, accessible fruit, ally transfer or established power-up may change newly supplied emission. The opponent may respond if time remains. No guaranteed turn before an overwhelming beam arrives. A mouth blast conflicts with eating; energy received is counted once.

Detached attacks cannot retroactively gain a later transformation. Merged beams add contributions actually arriving at the same collision; separated attacks use the shared-defence model. A counter selection can lead to interception, but collision and a direct body hit are different outcomes; never award both from one roll.

Preparation and activation use discrete15second tier anchors, independent of Power Level or movement speed. Costs retain their own interpolation. Combat uses range bands and effort-weighted positioning, not metres divided by Max Speed. Actual access and executable attacks can interrupt a charge; movement cannot shorten preparation.

Same-state residual reactivation lasts 15 minutes (900 seconds, inclusive) from the last exit from that particular form or Kaioken phase, including a forced exhaustion collapse. Once conscious and physically able to act with sufficient Endurance, the fighter may re-enter immediately within that window; afterward normal mastery-based activation applies. Record each state's last exit and expiry separately. Re-entry resumes ordinary upkeep and requires actual access, compatibility and supply. It restores no Endurance, Kiai buildup or attack charge, and grants no voluntary access to an involuntary state. Attacks always require fresh preparation.

sections.title: Technique Charge & Sensing
sections.summary: Attack factors belong to each technique; mastery controls accessible extra charge.
paragraphs: Regular Kamehameha is ×2; Galick Gun ×3; Spirit Spear ×2. Their full profile ceilings are ×4, ×6 and ×4 respectively. Additional charge accesses 25%, 50%, 75% or 100% of the gap above regular output at Learned, Proficient, Advanced or Mastered. These profiles do not assert that Zero has unlocked their peaks.

Kamehameha tier peaks are ×2.5/3/3.5/4; Galick Gun ×3.75/4.5/5.25/6; Spirit Spear ×2.5/3/3.5/4. Output rises linearly through the accessible extra-charge interval; do not multiply regular output by the total factor again. Timers require the recorded mastery tier and any evidenced individual exception before use.

Cannon has intrinsic14 before Mastered/15 at Mastered and cost40/32/24/18 times attained multiplier/3. Spirit Bomb has intrinsic19 before Mastered/20 at Mastered, regular×1, finite tier ceilings10/20/40/80, setup30/15/15/15 and total full600/480/360/300seconds. Collection rate is capacity divided by the full-minus-setup interval. Cost=economy*(4*setup_fraction+2*sqrt(collected/pre-technique Power Level)+2*collection_minutes), paid once. Actual supply can lengthen gathering; donors cannot bypass containment. Beyond mastery, capacity and rate grow by1+log2(1+extra/10000), with15second-rounded timing refinement; there is no universal lifetime ceiling.

Spirit Spear needs contact and actual gathered spirit energy; the timer cannot create supply. Energy enters at contact, mixes violently with the target’s body and ki, and can erupt from the opposite side when properly coupled. A guarded or incomplete strike can leave a local burn. No automatic armour bypass, extra exit multiplier or retrospective wound. Spirit Bomb also requires actual donation.

Mastery improves movement and control within each method. Mobile beams can develop skilled evasive handling; committed gathering techniques retain concentration and supply limits. Spirit Spear can gather during its committed approach and strike, but cannot bank energy through unrelated fighting.

Ordinary Kaioken uses one technique per phase, each with its own cumulative10/250/2500/10000 progression. Master the preceding phase before attempting the next: ×2, ×3, ×4, ×5, ×10, ×15, ×20, ×30, ×40, ×50, ×75, ×100. Earlier phases remain usable. Eligible novice attempts retain the execution-failure rule; mastery never automatically unlocks the successor. Zero’s Kaioken x2 retains650 progress and existing art; Kaioken x3 is currently ineligible. Separately trained form compatibility remains required and Channel stacking remains unsafe.

Learned sensing gives familiar direction/signatures and broad relative strength; Proficient improves moving-signature tracking and estimates; Advanced estimates roughly one significant figure; Mastered reads precise accessible current output. Suppression, hidden reserve and unfamiliar divine/artificial energy still limit what can be read. Zero’s current sensing remains approximate.

abilityNotes.spirit-spear: Campaign profile: regular ×2; full-charge envelope ×4, limited by mastery and actual gathered supply. Contact and proper coupling are required for the opposite-side eruption; no automatic penetration. Full spirit gathering takes longer than comparable Kamehameha or Galick Gun charging. These are profile limits, not a new full-charge feat.
abilityNotes.kaioken-technique: Kaioken x2 is the current ×2 technique. Each later phase requires mastery of its predecessor and has separate progress; mastery does not remove bodily damage. Combining with another form requires its own compatibility training. Sealed Channel stacking remains unsafe.
abilityNotes.ki-sensing: The mastery ladder distinguishes broad sensing, moving-signature tracking, Advanced rounded estimates and Mastered precise readable output. Current sensing remains approximate; the scouter still supplies exact readings.
